questions.questionText: Your company stores millions of user-uploaded images in Cloud Storage. As the application grows, storage costs are increasing rapidly. Images older than 30 days are rarely accessed. What is the most automated and cost-effective way to manage this data growth?
options: Configure Object Lifecycle Management to transition objects older than 30 days to Nearline or Coldline storage.
Write a daily cron job on a Compute Engine VM to copy old images to a new bucket and delete the originals.
Enable Cloud Storage Autoclass to automatically delete objects older than 30 days.
Download the old images to a local on-premises server and delete them from the cloud.
correctAnswers: Configure Object Lifecycle Management to transition objects older than 30 days to Nearline or Coldline storage.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management allows you to automate data growth management by defining rules that automatically transition objects to colder, cheaper storage classes (like Nearline, Coldline, or Archive) once they reach a certain age.

why other options are wrong.Write a daily cron job on a Compute Engi: This introduces operational overhead, compute costs, and potential for failure when a native, fully managed feature (Lifecycle Management) already exists.
why other options are wrong.Enable Cloud Storage Autoclass to automa: Autoclass transitions storage classes based on access patterns, but it does not automatically delete data. Lifecycle management is explicitly designed for transitioning based on age rules.
why other options are wrong.Download the old images to a local on-pr: This defeats the purpose of cloud storage, requires managing local hardware, and incurs high egress network costs.

questions.questionText: You are configuring a new Cloud SQL for MySQL database for a fast-growing startup. The data volume is expected to grow unpredictably over the next year. How can you ensure the database does not run out of disk space without manually monitoring and resizing the disk?
options: Enable the 'Automatic storage increase' feature in Cloud SQL.
Provision 64 TB of storage upfront to guarantee enough space.
Attach a new Persistent Disk to the Cloud SQL instance when alerts trigger.
Configure a Cloud Function to restart the database and clear old logs.
correctAnswers: Enable the 'Automatic storage increase' feature in Cloud SQL.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud SQL provides an 'Automatic storage increase' feature. When enabled, Google Cloud automatically adds storage capacity to the instance when it approaches its maximum limit, ensuring zero downtime and preventing out-of-disk errors as data grows.

why other options are wrong.Provision 64 TB of storage upfront to gu: Provisioning massive amounts of storage upfront incurs unnecessary costs for unused capacity.
why other options are wrong.Attach a new Persistent Disk to the Clou: Cloud SQL is a managed service; you cannot manually attach raw Persistent Disks to the underlying VM.
why other options are wrong.Configure a Cloud Function to restart th: Restarting the database causes downtime and clearing logs does not solve the root issue of actual database table data growth.

questions.questionText: Your application runs on a Compute Engine virtual machine and writes log files to an attached Persistent Disk. The disk is currently 500 GB and is 95% full. What is the simplest way to accommodate further data growth without experiencing application downtime?
options: Increase the size of the Persistent Disk in the Google Cloud Console, then resize the file system within the VM OS.
Create a new 1 TB Persistent Disk, attach it to the VM, and copy all data over using the command line.
Stop the VM, change the machine type to one with more local storage, and restart it.
You cannot increase the size of an existing Persistent Disk; you must delete old data.
correctAnswers: Increase the size of the Persistent Disk in the Google Cloud Console, then resize the file system within the VM OS.

explanation.general explanation: Google Cloud allows you to dynamically increase the size of a Persistent Disk while it is attached to a running VM and without downtime. After expanding the physical disk in the GCP console or CLI, you simply run a command inside the guest OS to resize the file system to use the new space.

why other options are wrong.Create a new 1 TB Persistent Disk, attac: While possible, this is much more complex and time-consuming than dynamically resizing the existing disk.
why other options are wrong.Stop the VM, change the machine type to: Machine types define CPU and RAM, not the size of attached Persistent Disks. Local SSDs are ephemeral and not meant for durable log storage.
why other options are wrong.You cannot increase the size of an exist: This is false. Persistent Disks can be easily scaled up.

questions.questionText: You are streaming massive amounts of analytics data into BigQuery every day. The total size of the dataset is growing by terabytes monthly. How does BigQuery automatically help manage the storage costs for historical data as it grows older?
options: BigQuery automatically cuts the storage price by 50% for any data that has not been modified for 90 consecutive days.
BigQuery automatically deletes data older than 365 days unless you pay a premium.
BigQuery compresses data older than 30 days, which makes querying slower but halves the cost.
BigQuery automatically exports data older than 90 days to Cloud Storage Archive.
correctAnswers: BigQuery automatically cuts the storage price by 50% for any data that has not been modified for 90 consecutive days.

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery has a built-in cost management feature for data growth: long-term storage pricing. Any table or partition that has not been edited or modified for 90 consecutive days automatically drops in storage price by approximately 50%, without any degradation in performance.

why other options are wrong.BigQuery automatically deletes data olde: BigQuery does not automatically delete data unless you explicitly configure a table expiration policy.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery compresses data older than 30 d: BigQuery data is already highly compressed in the Capacitor format. Long-term storage does not degrade query performance.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery automatically exports data olde: BigQuery does not automatically move your data to Cloud Storage; it keeps it in BigQuery but lowers the billing rate.

questions.questionText: Which TWO database services in Google Cloud natively support seamless horizontal scaling (adding more nodes) to accommodate virtually unbounded data growth and throughput? (Select two)
options: Cloud Spanner
Cloud Bigtable
Cloud SQL
Memorystore for Redis
Firestore in Datastore mode
correctAnswers: Cloud Spanner
Cloud Bigtable

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner (relational) and Cloud Bigtable (NoSQL wide-column) are designed from the ground up for massive, horizontal scalability. As your data and traffic grow, you simply add more nodes to the cluster to handle the load linearly.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a traditional relational database (MySQL, PostgreSQL) that primarily scales vertically (scaling up CPU/RAM), though it supports read replicas. It does not scale writes horizontally.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore for Redis: Memorystore is an in-memory cache and has hard limits on vertical instance size, not designed for unbounded persistent data growth.
why other options are wrong.Firestore in Datastore mode: While Firestore scales automatically, you do not 'add nodes' to it as it is a fully serverless document database. Bigtable and Spanner explicitly allow node-based horizontal scaling.

questions.questionText: TerramEarth (Case Study) expects their IoT sensor data to grow to petabytes over the next few years. They only need to actively query the last 30 days of data, and anything older can be permanently discarded to save costs. How should they manage this data growth in Cloud Bigtable?
options: Configure a Garbage Collection policy with a max age (TTL) of 30 days.
Write a daily Dataflow job to delete rows older than 30 days.
Use Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management to delete the Bigtable backup files.
Manually truncate the Bigtable tables on the first of every month.
correctAnswers: Configure a Garbage Collection policy with a max age (TTL) of 30 days.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Bigtable supports Garbage Collection policies. You can set a Time-To-Live (TTL) rule (e.g., max age of 30 days) at the column family level. Bigtable will automatically and efficiently delete data older than the TTL in the background, making it perfect for managing time-series data growth.

why other options are wrong.Write a daily Dataflow job to delete row: This introduces unnecessary compute costs and complexity when Bigtable has a native, automated feature for this exact use case.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Manag: This manages backup files in Cloud Storage, not the active, growing data inside the Bigtable database itself.
why other options are wrong.Manually truncate the Bigtable tables on: Truncating the table deletes all data, not just data older than 30 days, and doing it manually is an operational anti-pattern.

questions.questionText: Which TWO features in BigQuery are primarily used to maintain high query performance and control query costs as a table grows to petabytes in size? (Select two)
options: Partitioning
Clustering
Object Lifecycle Management
Read Replicas
Garbage Collection
correctAnswers: Partitioning
Clustering

explanation.general explanation: As BigQuery tables grow massively, querying the entire table becomes slow and expensive. Partitioning divides the table into segments (usually by date), allowing queries to scan only specific days. Clustering sorts the data within those partitions, further speeding up queries and reducing costs.

why other options are wrong.Object Lifecycle Management: This is a feature of Cloud Storage, not BigQuery.
why other options are wrong.Read Replicas: This is a feature of Cloud SQL to scale read traffic, not a BigQuery table structure optimization.
why other options are wrong.Garbage Collection: This is a feature of Cloud Bigtable for data deletion, not BigQuery query optimization.

questions.questionText: Your application writes to a Persistent Disk, and you receive an alert that the disk is 99% full. To accommodate immediate data growth without losing existing data or experiencing downtime, which TWO actions can you take? (Select two)
options: Increase the size of the existing Persistent Disk.
Attach a new Persistent Disk to the VM.
Decrease the size of the Persistent Disk to trigger auto-scaling.
Change the disk type from Standard to SSD to compress the data.
Convert the Persistent Disk into a Cloud Storage bucket.
correctAnswers: Increase the size of the existing Persistent Disk.
Attach a new Persistent Disk to the VM.

explanation.general explanation: When a Persistent Disk is full, you can easily handle the data growth by either dynamically increasing the size of the existing attached disk, or by provisioning a brand new disk and attaching it to the VM to use as additional storage space.

why other options are wrong.Decrease the size of the Persistent Disk: You cannot decrease the size of a Persistent Disk, and doing so would not trigger auto-scaling to add space anyway.
why other options are wrong.Change the disk type from Standard to SS: Changing disk types changes performance characteristics (IOPS/throughput) but does not compress data or magically increase free space.
why other options are wrong.Convert the Persistent Disk into a Cloud: These are fundamentally different storage types (block storage vs. object storage) and cannot be seamlessly converted into one another on a running VM.

questions.questionText: A team accidentally expanded a Persistent Disk to 10 TB instead of 1 TB. They realized the mistake and want to shrink the disk back to 1 TB to avoid high monthly costs. What is the correct procedure to achieve this?
options: Create a new 1 TB disk, copy the data from the 10 TB disk to the new disk, and delete the 10 TB disk.
Use the Google Cloud Console to simply edit the disk size and change it from 10 TB to 1 TB.
Run a file system shrink command in the VM OS, and Google Cloud will automatically adjust the billing.
Change the disk type to Cloud Storage Archive to stop billing for the unused 9 TB.
correctAnswers: Create a new 1 TB disk, copy the data from the 10 TB disk to the new disk, and delete the 10 TB disk.

explanation.general explanation: In Google Cloud, you cannot shrink the size of a Persistent Disk. Once expanded, the capacity is fixed at the new larger size. To reduce storage space and costs, you must provision a new, smaller disk, manually migrate the data over, and delete the large disk.

why other options are wrong.Use the Google Cloud Console to simply e: The GCP console will block you from entering a size smaller than the current disk size.
why other options are wrong.Run a file system shrink command in the: Billing is based on the provisioned disk size at the infrastructure layer, not how much space the OS file system thinks it is using.
why other options are wrong.Change the disk type to Cloud Storage Ar: Persistent Disks are block storage and cannot be converted into an Archive object storage class.

questions.questionText: Which Google Cloud storage service provides an unstructured object store that requires zero upfront capacity provisioning and automatically scales to handle exabytes of data growth natively?
options: Cloud Storage
Persistent Disk
Filestore
Cloud SQL
correctAnswers: Cloud Storage

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage is a highly scalable object storage service. You do not need to provision capacity or specify disk sizes upfront; it scales infinitely and automatically as you add objects to a bucket, making it ideal for unpredictable data growth.

why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk: Persistent Disk requires you to specify a fixed disk size (e.g., 500 GB) when creating it.
why other options are wrong.Filestore: Filestore requires you to provision a specific capacity tier and size for the NFS file share.
why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL requires provisioning storage space, although it has an auto-increase feature, it is still bounded and not designed for exabyte-scale unstructured data.

questions.questionText: EHR Healthcare (Case Study) generates millions of patient records that must be retained for 7 years to meet regulatory compliance. As the volume of historical records grows, storage costs are becoming a concern. These records are accessed less than once a year. Which storage class is the most appropriate for managing this long-term growth?
options: Cloud Storage Archive
Cloud Storage Standard
Persistent Disk Standard
Cloud Spanner
correctAnswers: Cloud Storage Archive

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage Archive is the lowest-cost storage class in Google Cloud. It is designed specifically for long-term data retention, compliance archiving, and disaster recovery where data is accessed less than once a year.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage Standard: Standard storage is intended for frequently accessed 'hot' data and is far too expensive for data accessed once a year.
why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk Standard: Persistent Disk provides block storage for VMs and is too expensive and complex for long-term, compliance archiving.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Spanner: Cloud Spanner is a highly performant, global relational database, not an archiving service for cold file storage.

questions.questionText: Which TWO actions can be automatically performed by Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management to manage data growth and optimize costs? (Select two)
options: SetStorageClass (e.g., transition to Coldline)
Delete
Compress to ZIP format
Move to a different geographic region
Encrypt with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK)
correctAnswers: SetStorageClass (e.g., transition to Coldline)
Delete

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management supports two primary actions when conditions (like object age) are met: `SetStorageClass`, which transitions the object to a colder, cheaper storage tier, and `Delete`, which permanently removes the object.

why other options are wrong.Compress to ZIP format: Lifecycle management cannot alter the actual content or format of the files.
why other options are wrong.Move to a different geographic region: Lifecycle rules change storage classes or delete objects within the same bucket; they do not migrate objects to buckets in other regions.
why other options are wrong.Encrypt with Customer-Managed Encryption: Encryption settings are configured at the bucket level or object creation time, not dynamically changed as a lifecycle action based on age.

questions.questionText: Your application uses a Cloud Spanner database. Due to a successful marketing campaign, your user base has tripled in the last week, resulting in sustained high CPU utilization. How do you scale the database to accommodate this massive growth?
options: Increase the compute capacity by adding more nodes (or processing units) to the Spanner instance.
Enable the 'Automatic storage increase' toggle in the Google Cloud console.
Change the Spanner instance machine type from n1-standard to n2-highcpu.
Migrate the database to Cloud SQL to take advantage of read replicas.
correctAnswers: Increase the compute capacity by adding more nodes (or processing units) to the Spanner instance.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner scales horizontally. To handle increased throughput and reduce CPU utilization, you simply increase the compute capacity of your instance by adding more nodes or processing units. Spanner automatically distributes the load across the new capacity without downtime.

why other options are wrong.Enable the 'Automatic storage increase': This is a feature of Cloud SQL, not Cloud Spanner. Furthermore, the issue is high CPU (compute constraint), not running out of disk space.
why other options are wrong.Change the Spanner instance machine type: You do not select underlying GCE machine types for Spanner; you manage capacity via abstract nodes/processing units.
why other options are wrong.Migrate the database to Cloud SQL to tak: Cloud Spanner is far more scalable than Cloud SQL. Downgrading to Cloud SQL would be detrimental to handling massive growth.

questions.questionText: Your e-commerce application uses a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database. The data size is stable, but heavy user traffic is causing slow query responses because the database is overwhelmed by simultaneous read requests. What is the best way to handle this traffic growth?
options: Add Read Replicas to the Cloud SQL instance.
Enable 'Automatic storage increase'.
Change the disk type from SSD to HDD.
Implement Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle rules.
correctAnswers: Add Read Replicas to the Cloud SQL instance.

explanation.general explanation: Adding Read Replicas allows you to scale out the read capacity of your Cloud SQL database. By offloading read-only queries (like fetching product catalogs) to the replicas, you relieve pressure on the primary database, effectively handling read traffic growth.

This feature adds disk space when the database is full; it does not increase CPU/memory capacity to handle high read query throughput.
Downgrading from SSD to HDD would drastically reduce IOPS and make the database perform much worse.
why other options are wrong.Implement Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle: Cloud Storage lifecycle rules have nothing to do with relational Cloud SQL databases.

questions.questionText: You have enabled Object Versioning on a Cloud Storage bucket to protect against accidental overwrites. However, because objects are updated frequently, the total storage cost is growing exponentially as old versions accumulate. How can you automate cost management for this bucket?
options: Create a Lifecycle Management rule to delete noncurrent object versions after a specific number of days.
Disable Object Versioning, as it cannot be used cost-effectively with frequently updated objects.
Configure the bucket to use the Ephemeral storage class.
Use a VPC firewall rule to block the overwrite API calls.
correctAnswers: Create a Lifecycle Management rule to delete noncurrent object versions after a specific number of days.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management includes conditions specifically for versioned objects (like `numNewerVersions` or `daysSinceNoncurrentTime`). This allows you to automatically delete or archive old, noncurrent versions to control data growth and storage costs effectively.

why other options are wrong.Disable Object Versioning, as it cannot: Disabling versioning removes the protection against accidental overwrites, which defeats the business requirement. Lifecycle rules solve the cost issue.
why other options are wrong.Configure the bucket to use the Ephemera: There is no 'Ephemeral' storage class in Cloud Storage.
why other options are wrong.Use a VPC firewall rule to block the ove: VPC firewall rules control network traffic; they cannot block specific Cloud Storage API operations.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a legacy application that relies on the NFS protocol to Google Cloud. The application requires file storage that can scale in capacity and performance as the amount of user data grows over time. Which Google Cloud service should you choose?
options: Filestore
Cloud Storage
Persistent Disk
Memorystore
correctAnswers: Filestore

explanation.general explanation: Filestore is Google Cloud's fully managed Network Attached Storage (NAS) service providing a standard NFS interface. It allows you to provision file shares and scale their capacity up as your data grows, making it the perfect target for legacy NFS applications.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage is an object store. While it can be mounted using Cloud Storage FUSE, it does not natively behave exactly like a highly performant NFS file system for legacy apps.
why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk: Persistent Disks provide block storage to a single VM (or multi-writer in specific modes), but they do not provide a managed NFS service.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore: Memorystore is an in-memory Redis/Memcached service, not a durable file storage system.

questions.questionText: When planning for massive data growth, it is crucial to understand the limitations of individual services. What is the maximum size a single standard Persistent Disk can be scaled to when attached to a Compute Engine virtual machine?
options: 64 TB
1 TB
10 TB
Unlimited
correctAnswers: 64 TB

explanation.general explanation: In Google Cloud, a single Persistent Disk (standard, balanced, or SSD) can be sized up to a maximum of 64 TB. If your data grows beyond this limit, you must attach multiple disks or use a different storage service.

why other options are wrong.1 TB: This is too low; PDs support up to 64 TB.
why other options are wrong.10 TB: This is too low; PDs support up to 64 TB.
why other options are wrong.Unlimited: Persistent Disks are bounded block storage devices. Only Cloud Storage offers virtually unlimited object storage.

questions.questionText: Your application stores configuration files in a Cloud Storage bucket. You only want to apply an Object Lifecycle Management rule to delete files that start with the word 'temp_'. How can you achieve this without affecting other files in the bucket?
options: Use a Prefix condition in the Lifecycle rule matching 'temp_'.
Place the files in a separate bucket; lifecycle rules apply to the whole bucket blindly.
Use a Cloud Function to rename the files, which automatically deletes them.
Use a Tag condition matching 'temporary' in the Lifecycle rule.
correctAnswers: Use a Prefix condition in the Lifecycle rule matching 'temp_'.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Storage Object Lifecycle Management rules can be finely tuned using conditions. The 'MatchesPrefix' (or Prefix) condition allows you to apply lifecycle actions (like Delete or SetStorageClass) only to objects whose names begin with a specific string, such as 'temp_'.

why other options are wrong.Place the files in a separate bucket; li: This is false; lifecycle rules can be scoped using conditions like Prefix and Suffix.
why other options are wrong.Use a Cloud Function to rename the files: Renaming files does not delete them automatically. Using built-in lifecycle conditions is the standard approach.
why other options are wrong.Use a Tag condition matching 'temporary': Lifecycle rules are not based on user-defined tags; they use native conditions like Age, Prefix, Suffix, and Storage Class.

questions.questionText: You are migrating a massive 50 TB on-premises media archive to Google Cloud. The data volume will continue to grow, and you need a robust, managed way to schedule the initial transfer and ongoing daily delta syncs to a Cloud Storage bucket. Which service is designed for this?
options: Storage Transfer Service
Cloud Dataflow
gsutil running on a local laptop
Cloud Storage FUSE
correctAnswers: Storage Transfer Service

explanation.general explanation: Storage Transfer Service allows you to automate the transfer of data from on-premises locations (using transfer agents) or from other clouds into Google Cloud Storage. It handles scheduling, retries, and delta syncs natively, making it perfect for migrating and managing growing archives.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: Dataflow is for processing and transforming data pipelines, not specifically for migrating raw files from an on-premises NAS to Cloud Storage.
why other options are wrong.gsutil running on a local laptop: While gsutil works, running it on a local laptop is not robust, scalable, or fully managed for a massive 50 TB transfer with scheduled delta syncs.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage FUSE: Cloud Storage FUSE allows you to mount a bucket as a local file system; it is not a data transfer scheduling tool.

questions.questionText: If you enable 'Automatic storage increase' on a Cloud SQL instance to plan for future data growth, does the database experience downtime when the storage auto-scales?
options: No, the storage capacity is added online without requiring a restart or downtime.
Yes, the database must restart to recognize the new disk size.
Yes, but only for replica instances; the primary remains online.
No, but the database goes into read-only mode for 10 minutes.
correctAnswers: No, the storage capacity is added online without requiring a restart or downtime.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud SQL's automatic storage increase is a seamless operation. When the storage threshold is reached, Google Cloud dynamically adds disk space to the instance online, with zero downtime and without placing the database in read-only mode.

why other options are wrong.Yes, the database must restart to recogn: This is false; the resize is handled dynamically at the infrastructure layer.
why other options are wrong.Yes, but only for replica instances; the: Neither primary nor replicas require downtime for storage increases.
why other options are wrong.No, but the database goes into read-only: There is no read-only window during a storage expansion.

questions.questionText: Your company is deploying a stateful application on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that stores user data on Persistent Volumes. You anticipate the data will grow over time. What must be true about the StorageClass configuration to allow expanding the volumes later?
options: The StorageClass must have `allowVolumeExpansion` set to `true`.
The StorageClass must be set to use Local SSDs.
The StorageClass must have `volumeBindingMode` set to `Immediate`.
The StorageClass must use the NFS provisioner.
correctAnswers: The StorageClass must have `allowVolumeExpansion` set to `true`.

explanation.general explanation: In Kubernetes, to dynamically resize a Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) to accommodate data growth without losing data, the underlying StorageClass must explicitly have the `allowVolumeExpansion: true` property configured.

why other options are wrong.The StorageClass must be set to use Loca: Local SSDs are ephemeral and cannot be dynamically resized like network-attached Persistent Disks.
why other options are wrong.The StorageClass must have `volumeBindin: Volume binding mode affects when the volume is provisioned (e.g., waiting for pod scheduling), but does not dictate whether the volume can be expanded later.
why other options are wrong.The StorageClass must use the NFS provis: Volume expansion works natively with standard GCE Persistent Disks (block storage); it does not require an NFS provisioner.

questions.questionText: Which TWO of the following Cloud Storage classes are explicitly designed to cost-effectively manage data growth for historical, infrequently accessed data? (Select two)
options: Coldline Storage
Archive Storage
Standard Storage
Multi-Regional Storage
Local SSD Storage
correctAnswers: Coldline Storage
Archive Storage

explanation.general explanation: Coldline Storage (for data accessed less than once a quarter) and Archive Storage (for data accessed less than once a year) provide highly durable object storage at significantly lower per-GB prices, making them the standard choices for managing the growth of historical cold data.

why other options are wrong.Standard Storage: Standard storage is for 'hot', frequently accessed data and has higher storage costs.
why other options are wrong.Multi-Regional Storage: This is a legacy term now bundled into Standard storage concepts, primarily focused on geo-redundancy of hot data.
why other options are wrong.Local SSD Storage: This is ephemeral, extremely fast block storage attached to VMs, completely unsuitable for long-term data archiving.

questions.questionText: Mountkirk Games (Case Study) captures massive amounts of game telemetry data. As the game becomes popular globally, they need a database that can handle millions of writes per second and grow from gigabytes to petabytes without architectural changes. Which service is best suited?
options: Cloud Bigtable
Cloud SQL
Memorystore
Cloud Storage
correctAnswers: Cloud Bigtable

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database specifically designed for massive scale, high-throughput time-series data (like gaming telemetry), and low-latency writes. It scales linearly by adding nodes as data grows to petabytes.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a relational database and cannot scale horizontally to handle millions of writes per second.
why other options are wrong.Memorystore: Memorystore is an in-memory cache, not a persistent database for petabyte-scale historical telemetry.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: While Cloud Storage holds petabytes of data, it is an object store, not a database capable of sub-millisecond querying and time-series write throughput.

questions.questionText: A data engineering team is using BigQuery as their enterprise data warehouse. They are worried about managing storage quotas and provisioning new disks as their data lake grows from 10 TB to 100 TB. What should you advise them regarding BigQuery's storage provisioning?
options: BigQuery storage is fully managed and auto-scales indefinitely; no upfront capacity provisioning is required.
They must purchase a 100 TB BigQuery Storage Reservation in the console.
They must attach additional Persistent Disks to the BigQuery cluster as data grows.
BigQuery has a hard limit of 50 TB; they must shard the data across multiple projects.
correctAnswers: BigQuery storage is fully managed and auto-scales indefinitely; no upfront capacity provisioning is required.

explanation.general explanation: BigQuery is a fully serverless data warehouse. You do not provision servers or storage disks. Storage automatically scales in the background as you load more data into your tables, making data growth management effortless.

why other options are wrong.They must purchase a 100 TB BigQuery Sto: Reservations in BigQuery are primarily for compute capacity (slots/flat-rate billing), not for allocating storage space.
why other options are wrong.They must attach additional Persistent D: You do not manage the underlying VMs or disks for BigQuery; it is completely serverless.
why other options are wrong.BigQuery has a hard limit of 50 TB; they: BigQuery easily handles petabytes and exabytes of data; there is no 50 TB limit.

questions.questionText: As a global application's user base grows, read latency becomes an issue for users far away from the primary Cloud Spanner region. How can you plan for this geographical data access growth?
options: Upgrade the Cloud Spanner instance from a regional to a multi-region configuration.
Create Cloud Storage buckets in other regions and export Spanner backups there.
Use Cloud CDN to cache all Cloud Spanner database queries at the edge.
Enable the 'Auto-scaling regional' feature in the GCP console.
correctAnswers: Upgrade the Cloud Spanner instance from a regional to a multi-region configuration.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Spanner can be deployed in multi-region configurations. This automatically replicates your database across multiple geographic regions, providing read-replicas close to users worldwide and protecting against entire region failures.

why other options are wrong.Create Cloud Storage buckets in other re: Backups are for disaster recovery, they do not help serve live, low-latency reads to global users.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud CDN to cache all Cloud Spanner: Cloud CDN caches static web assets (like images) over HTTP, it cannot cache complex, dynamic Spanner SQL queries natively.
why other options are wrong.Enable the 'Auto-scaling regional' featu: There is no feature by this name that solves global read latency.

questions.questionText: Your organization wants to ensure they always have Compute Engine capacity available in a specific zone to accommodate anticipated rapid growth during a holiday season. How can you guarantee this compute capacity is held for you, even if you haven't launched the VMs yet?
options: Create a Compute Engine Capacity Reservation in that zone.
Purchase a 3-year Committed Use Discount (CUD).
Preemptively launch the VMs and pause them.
Configure a Managed Instance Group with auto-scaling.
correctAnswers: Create a Compute Engine Capacity Reservation in that zone.

explanation.general explanation: Compute Engine Capacity Reservations allow you to guarantee that resources (vCPUs, memory, GPUs) are available in a specific zone when you need them. You pay for the reserved resources whether they are actively used by a VM or not.

why other options are wrong.Purchase a 3-year Committed Use Discount: CUDs provide a financial discount for committing to usage, but they do NOT guarantee physical hardware capacity availability in a specific zone during peak times.
why other options are wrong.Preemptively launch the VMs and pause th: While possible, managing stopped/paused VMs is operationally messy compared to using native Capacity Reservations.
why other options are wrong.Configure a Managed Instance Group with: MIGs automatically scale based on load, but if the zone experiences a severe capacity shortage, the MIG might fail to provision new VMs. Reservations guarantee the capacity.

questions.questionText: Which TWO settings can be configured in a Cloud Bigtable Garbage Collection policy to automatically delete old data and manage unbounded data growth? (Select two)
options: Max age (Time-To-Live / TTL)
Max number of versions
Min row size (Bytes)
Max CPU utilization percentage
Idle time limit
correctAnswers: Max age (Time-To-Live / TTL)
Max number of versions

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Bigtable manages data growth at the cell level using Garbage Collection policies. You can configure rules based on 'Max age' (e.g., delete data older than 30 days) and/or 'Max number of versions' (e.g., only keep the 3 most recent updates to a cell).

why other options are wrong.Min row size (Bytes): Bigtable garbage collection policies are based on age and versions, not on the physical byte size of the row.
why other options are wrong.Max CPU utilization percentage: This is a metric used for auto-scaling cluster nodes, not for garbage collecting old data.
why other options are wrong.Idle time limit: There is no setting to delete data based on how long it has been 'idle' or unqueried in Bigtable.

questions.questionText: A startup is building a mobile application. The data model is highly flexible and the user profile schema changes weekly. They anticipate massive, rapid data growth and want a fully managed NoSQL database that scales to zero when unused but can handle millions of documents seamlessly. Which service fits best?
options: Firestore
Cloud SQL
Cloud Bigtable
Persistent Disk
correctAnswers: Firestore

explanation.general explanation: Firestore is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL document database. It is ideal for flexible schemas (like user profiles), provides built-in mobile SDKs, and automatically scales compute and storage seamlessly as data grows, even scaling to zero when inactive.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL requires strict relational schemas and does not scale to zero natively without stopping the instance.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Bigtable: While highly scalable, Bigtable is not meant for flexible mobile document queries; it is for heavy, flat, wide-column time-series data.
why other options are wrong.Persistent Disk: Persistent Disk is block storage for VMs, not a managed NoSQL database.

questions.questionText: Your Cloud SQL instance currently has a 500 GB disk. The 'Automatic storage increase' feature is NOT enabled. If your data grows to exactly 500 GB, what happens to the database?
options: The database will stop accepting write operations until you manually increase the storage size.
Cloud SQL will automatically delete the oldest records to make space.
Google Cloud will force-enable the automatic storage increase feature to prevent downtime.
The database will compress the existing data to make 10% more room.
correctAnswers: The database will stop accepting write operations until you manually increase the storage size.

explanation.general explanation: If 'Automatic storage increase' is disabled and a Cloud SQL instance runs out of disk space, the database becomes full and will reject any new write/insert operations (resulting in application errors) until an administrator manually increases the disk size.

why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL will automatically delete the: Cloud SQL will never delete customer table data automatically to free up space.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud will force-enable the autom: Google does not override user configuration. If auto-increase is disabled, it stays disabled.
why other options are wrong.The database will compress the existing: There is no native mechanism that suddenly compresses data on a full disk to prevent a crash.

questions.questionText: You are hosting a static website using a Cloud Storage bucket. Over the years, you have updated the HTML and image files hundreds of times. You have Object Versioning enabled. To prevent storage costs from growing infinitely due to these updates, what is the best practice?
options: Use Object Lifecycle Management to keep only the 3 most recent versions of an object.
Manually delete the entire bucket and recreate it every year.
Change the bucket's storage class to Archive to make all versions cheap.
Turn off Object Versioning, which automatically deletes all previous versions.
correctAnswers: Use Object Lifecycle Management to keep only the 3 most recent versions of an object.

explanation.general explanation: Object Lifecycle Management allows you to specify the `numNewerVersions` condition. Setting this to 3 ensures that only the 3 most recent noncurrent versions of an object are retained, automatically deleting older versions and preventing infinite storage cost growth while still providing rollback capability.

why other options are wrong.Manually delete the entire bucket and re: This would cause downtime for the website and is an extreme, unmanaged approach.
why other options are wrong.Change the bucket's storage class to Arc: Archive storage has high retrieval costs and minimum retention periods, making it terrible for active static website hosting.
why other options are wrong.Turn off Object Versioning, which automa: Turning off versioning simply stops creating new versions; it does NOT automatically delete existing historical versions.
